```markdown
# lock-closures roadmap

## Outcomes

Source: partner's words, 2026-11-06. Background: none.
Choices made: none.

| # | Outcome | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | How the chance that a lock closes moves with the upstream river-gauge level | A | 1 | measured by Stage 1 |
| O2 | A 7-day closure-risk outlook for each lock from the river-level forecast | A | 2 | one model run a day, small once O1's model exists; basis: Stage 1's measured fit time |
| O3 | Separate closure curves for all 14 locks, pooled across locks | A | 3 | about 14× Stage 1's data; basis: Stage 1's measured data volume |
| O4 | A closure-history map for the canal's boat operators | A | 4 | about a day of work; basis: one static map page |

Tracks: A — closure risk from river level (research). One track, confirmed by partner 2026-11-06.

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Closure chance vs upstream gauge level
      Objective: Estimate, on real closure records and real upstream gauge readings, how the chance that a lock closes moves with the gauge level.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: nothing (the package is an empty scaffold)
      Produces: specs/lock-closures-stage-1-findings.md, holding the estimated relationship and the measured cost of the real run
      Exit: O1 — a closure-chance-vs-gauge-level relationship, with its uncertainty, estimated from real data and recorded in the findings file; the findings file records the real run's wall time, compute and data volume
      Leaves out: traceability: suggested, see the approval question
      ROUTING: brainstorming

## Ranked list — Track A
1. O2 — one model run a day, small once O1's model exists; basis: Stage 1's measured fit time
2. O3 — about 14× Stage 1's data; basis: Stage 1's measured data volume
3. O4 — about a day of work; basis: one static map page

## Stage-spec stamp

Every stage spec's Rollout note carries this line, which writing-plans copies verbatim into the stage plan's header:

> Roadmap: specs/lock-closures-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick the stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

When every committed stage is ticked and the Ranked list is empty, or parked, re-run the gap rubric over the Outcomes list (SKILL.md §6), with evidence per verdict. Unmet outcomes exit as a new stage or as a conscious deferral with a written why.
```

---

The roadmap is written to `specs/lock-closures-roadmap.md` and is **not committed yet**. It commits once you approve.

Track A is research, so only its core stage is committed. **Stage 1** delivers O1 on real data, routes to brainstorming, and records the measured cost of its run in `specs/lock-closures-stage-1-findings.md`. O2, O3 and O4 wait in the Ranked list in your order. That way Stage 1's finding and cost can inform the re-rank before any of them is promoted.

There is one quality I suggest adding. **Traceability**: the board will ask which gauge readings each closure estimate came from. If you approve it, it would become this outcome:

> **O5.** For each closure estimate, the gauge readings (gauge, time, value) it was computed from, ready to show the trust's board.

Stage 1 leaves it out in either case, so the core run stays at the smallest usable standard.

**One question:** do you approve this partition, and do you want traceability added as O5? If you do, where should it rank among O2–O4?

Once you answer, I'll record it in the file and commit on `main`. Then I'll give you the handoff line for Stage 1.
